_comment: Idea bank fed to the research and analysis agents. Hook patterns and structure are ADAPTED from vidIQ's public guidance (vidIQ is YouTube-focused, so entertainment topics are deliberately not copied: only hook mechanics and formats that fit the brand rules in services.json). Edit freely. 'ideas' are used in file order; an idea is skipped once a draft used it (draft.idea_id).
sources: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)'
vidIQ, '9 Video Ideas to Go Viral with YouTube Shorts'
vidIQ, '80 Best YouTube Niches for 2026' (AI-tool tutorials and trending-topic commentary rank among the most shared formats)

hook_library.note: this-or-that sparks a verdict; keep both sides fair
listicle: viewers expect quick, practical value

hook_library.pattern: Try this to ___ / A simple way to ___
hook_library.note: a small action the reader can do today
answers a real repeat question; never imply the owner has many clients
set the record straight; only with facts you can stand behind
caption-first, works on mute; one relatable moment

hook_library.pattern: Did you know ___? / Have you ever wondered ___?
hook_library.note: only with true, general facts; no invented statistics
an honest opinion that breaks the usual advice; explain why

hook_library.pattern: Show the result, then explain how
hook_library.note: open on the outcome, not the setup

hook_library.pattern: Wait for it / Watch what changes at 0:07
hook_library.note: only if the payoff really arrives; never bait and switch

reel_rules: The hook lands in about 1 second, not 3: people decide before the first sentence ends.
Stack three things in the first frame: a visual that shows the payoff (not the setup), 3-7 words of bold on-screen text in the top third, and a spoken line of 5-10 words.
One idea, one specific promise, and make clear who it is for (a small business owner) at once.
No greeting or brand intro ('Hello guys', 'Welcome back'): the first words are the problem or the result.
Deliver on the hook; the rest of the reel builds on the promise.
Make it work on mute: the on-screen text must carry the message without sound.
End so the last line or frame hands back to the first (for example, end on the question the opening line answers) so a replay feels natural.

ideas.hook: Instagram page vs website: which one earns trust?
ideas.topic: Instagram page vs website: what each can and cannot do for a small business
ideas.angle: A page is easy to find; a website answers 'is this business real?' with services, location and a contact button in one place.

ideas.hook: 3 things customers look for before they message you
ideas.topic: The 3 things a customer checks on your page before messaging
ideas.angle: What you sell, where you are, how to reach you. If one is missing, some visitors leave.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hook 15)

ideas.hook: Try this: open your own website on mobile data
ideas.topic: A quick mobile test for your own website
ideas.angle: On mobile data, can you find the call button without scrolling, and does the page load before you lose patience?
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hook 10)

ideas.hook: 3 questions every customer asks. Could a bot answer them?
ideas.topic: The repeat questions a chatbot can handle: price, location, timings
ideas.angle: Repeat questions eat the day. A bot handles those so the owner can spend time on real conversations.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hooks 7 and 15)

ideas.hook: Chatbot vs unanswered message: what does the customer see?
ideas.topic: What a customer experiences when a message goes unanswered versus getting a quick first reply
ideas.angle: A quick first reply keeps the conversation alive; the owner follows up on the rest. Use a clearly labelled example conversation.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hook 12)

ideas.hook: Myth: chatbots sound robotic. Fact: it depends on setup
ideas.topic: Chatbot myths: robotic tone and no human handover
ideas.angle: Tone comes from the instructions it is given, and a good setup hands over to the owner when it cannot answer.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '9 Video Ideas to Go Viral with YouTube Shorts' (myth-busting)

ideas.hook: The first second of your ad decides if it gets seen
ideas.topic: Planning the first second of an ad: payoff first, 3-7 words of text, no logo intro
ideas.angle: Open on the result, put a short line of text in the top third, and save the brand for the end.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (visual + text + verbal hook)

ideas.hook: Static post vs short animated ad: which stops the scroll?
ideas.topic: Why movement in the first second changes how people react to an ad
ideas.angle: Movement can catch the eye before words are read. One message, big text, one next step.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hook 12)

ideas.hook: POV: your ad is the fourth one they scrolled past
ideas.topic: Standing out in a crowded feed: one message, big text, movement
ideas.angle: People scroll fast; an ad that is clear in a glance has a chance.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (caption-first formats)

ideas.hook: 3 places to spot businesses that need your service
ideas.topic: Where freelancers and agencies look for businesses to pitch
ideas.angle: Local businesses in your city and category, with their contact details, review counts and website checks, plus newly opened ones. Whatever you sell, start from a list of real local businesses instead of a blank search. Speak to every freelancer and agency, not one profession.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (hook 15)

ideas.hook: POV: you've spent hours searching and have 5 leads
ideas.topic: The time cost of searching for leads by hand
ideas.angle: Cold-searching eats the time you could spend pitching. Do not state a price.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' (caption-first formats)

ideas.topic: Why a reel's first line should be the problem, not a greeting
ideas.angle: The opening words decide if people stay. Lead with the problem or the result, not a welcome.
ideas.source: vidIQ, '18 Viral Hooks for YouTube Shorts (2026 Guide)' ('never start with filler')

ideas.hook: A reel script in 3 lines: problem, proof, one step

ideas.angle: Problem first, one proof point, one clear next step (a DM keyword).

ideas.angle: Every repeat question is a blog post that can answer it before the customer has to message you.
